What makes an owl so amazing?

The owl, hunter of the night, is a mysterious bird with big eyes and a striking face. Its ability to swivel its head around and fly in complete silence is astonishing.

We've gathered all kinds of stories about owls — owl facts, owl behavior, and nocturnal birds.

content.text:
Nature and science facts about owls

An owl's round facial disc funnels sound into its ears, and because its ears are asymmetrical, it can pinpoint exactly where a sound is coming from. Its eyes are fixed facing forward, so it turns its head as far as about 270 degrees. Thanks to the comb-like structure of its feathers, it flies almost silently, so prey never notices. It swallows prey whole — bones and fur — then coughs up the parts it can't digest as a pellet, and it nests in tree holes.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Why does an owl turn its head so far?
A. Its eyes are fixed facing forward and can't roll around, so it turns its head about 270 degrees to look around.

Q. How does an owl fly silently?
A. Thanks to the comb-like structure of its feathers. It sneaks up quietly so prey never notices.

Q. How can we observe owls at home?
A. Compare head turns, watch a video of silent flight, and talk about pellets.
